ar-aiv.s: Ivan Aivazovsky loved to paint the sea more than anything in the world. He painted about six thousand pictures! The most famous one is “The Ninth Wave”. After a storm, sailors hold on to a piece of a broken mast. A huge wave rises above them, and so does the morning sun. Aivazovsky painted waves from memory. This painting is in the Russian Museum in Saint Petersburg.

ar-shishkin.s: Ivan Shishkin painted forests so well that you almost smell the pine needles. In “Morning in a Pine Forest”, a mother bear and her cubs play on a fallen pine tree. But here is a secret: Shishkin did not paint the bears. His friend, the artist Konstantin Savitsky, did. This painting is even on the wrapper of “Mishka Kosolapy” (“Clumsy Bear”) sweets.

ar-vasn.s: Viktor Vasnetsov loved Russian fairy tales and old hero stories very much. In his painting “The Bogatyrs” there are three strong heroes on horses. In the middle is Ilya Muromets. Beside him are Dobrynya Nikitich and Alyosha Popovich. They look far away. Is an enemy coming? Vasnetsov worked on this painting for almost thirty years!

ar-bryull.s: Almost two thousand years ago, the volcano Vesuvius woke up near the city of Pompeii. The artist Karl Bryullov went to see the place. He painted a huge picture of that day. People run away and help each other. Bryullov even painted himself in the picture: an artist with a box of paints on his head. This painting is in the Russian Museum.

ar-leo.s: Leonardo da Vinci was an artist, an inventor and a scientist. He painted the “Mona Lisa” with her secret smile. Leonardo thought up flying machines. He wrote down his ideas in mirror writing, from right to left. In the Hermitage in Saint Petersburg there are two of his paintings: the “Litta Madonna” and the “Benois Madonna”.
a: In mirror writing, from right to left

ar-vangogh.s: The Dutch artist Vincent van Gogh painted with thick lines of bright paint. In “The Starry Night”, the sky swirls round and round. The stars shine like lanterns. A yellow moon hangs above the hills. Van Gogh painted the view from his window, but he made up the sky himself. Try drawing your own sky with swirls!

ar-monet.s: The French artist Claude Monet loved to paint light: in the morning, in the evening, in sun and in mist. He had a garden with a pond and a Japanese bridge. Water lilies grew in the pond. Monet painted them again and again, about two hundred and fifty pictures! One of his paintings is called “Impression”. From that word came the name of a whole kind of art: Impressionism.

ar-kand.s: Wassily Kandinsky heard colours like music. To him, yellow sounded like a trumpet, and blue sounded like a cello. He did not paint houses and people. He painted circles, lines and blobs that look like music. He was one of the first artists to paint like this. Put on some music and draw how it sounds!

ar-malevich.s: Kazimir Malevich painted a black square on a white background. Many people were surprised. Is that a painting? But Malevich wanted to show that a picture can have no things in it, only shape and colour. “Black Square” became one of the most famous paintings in the world. One of its versions is in the Hermitage.

ph-swing.s: A swing goes back and forth, back and forth, like the swinging part inside an old clock. The higher you go, the faster you whoosh past at the very bottom. Height turns into speed. To swing without a push, use your body. When you fly forwards, lean back and stretch out your legs. When you fly backwards, lean forwards and tuck your legs in. To swing standing up, crouch at the ends of the swing and stand up straight at the bottom. It does not matter if you are heavy or light. On the same swing, everyone goes back and forth in the same time.
a: Where a cat is looking at you

ph-slide.s: On a slide, gravity pulls you down. Friction slows you down. Friction is when two things rub and grip each other. Bare legs grip the slide more than clothes do. So in shorts you go slower than in trousers. A smooth metal slide is usually slippery. A plastic slide with scratches slows you more. Water, like in a water park, works like oil: there is less friction, so you fly faster. And the steeper the slide, the harder gravity pulls you down it.
a: In shorts, with a sandwich in your hand

ph-seesaw.s: A seesaw is a long board with a stand in the middle. This kind of thing is called a lever. If Dad sits at one end and you sit at the other, Dad goes down and you hang in the air. But if Dad moves closer to the middle, the board becomes level! The farther you sit from the middle, the harder you press down on the board. So the heavy person sits closer to the middle, and the light person sits at the very end.
a: To the very end, and eat a pie
To the roof of the house next door

ph-carousel.s: On a spinning merry-go-round, it feels as if something pulls you out. But nobody is pushing you out. Your body wants to go in a straight line. This is called inertia. The merry-go-round keeps turning, and your hands on the bar pull you round in a circle. You feel it more at the edge than in the middle. If you let go of the bar, you would fly off in a straight line, the way you were going at that moment. So always hold on tight on a merry-go-round.
a: Your body wants to go straight
The merry-go-round got cross and is pushing you out
An invisible vacuum cleaner is pulling you

ph-trampoline.s: A trampoline is springy. If you stretch it, it tries to go back. When you land on it, the mat sinks down. It stores the energy of your fall, like a stretched elastic band. Then it flattens out again and throws you up. If you also push with your legs at the very bottom, you add your own energy and fly higher. To stop, bend your knees at the bottom. Then the trampoline soaks up your jump.
a: The springy mat that flattens out again
A little gnome under the trampoline

ph-ball.s: When a ball hits the ground, it gets squashed for a moment. The air inside is squeezed and pushes the sides back. The ball goes round again and bounces off. This is being springy. In a ball full of air, the air is squeezed harder. The ball dents less and loses less energy. A flat ball crumples like a rag. The energy goes into squashing the rubber and turns into heat. That is why a flat ball hardly bounces at all.
a: One that is full of air
A flat one, like a pancake
The one that had a good sleep today

ph-scooter.s: You go fast on a scooter, then you stop pushing, and it keeps rolling. That is inertia: anything that is moving wants to keep moving. Little by little, friction and the air slow it down. The brake stops it faster. It rubs the wheel and takes away speed. If you brake suddenly, your body flies forwards because of inertia. So brake gently and wear a helmet. It is also easier to keep your balance when you are moving. On a bike, if you start to lean to one side, you can turn the handlebars a little to that side.
a: It is hurrying to visit Granny
Squirrels are running in the wheels

ph-skate-ramp.s: On a skate ramp, energy keeps changing. At the top you are up high, and you have the energy of being high. You roll down. Height turns into speed, and at the bottom you go fastest. You ride up the other side. Speed turns back into height, and you slow down. Without a push, you cannot get higher than where you started. Friction and the air take some of the energy on the way.
a: At the very top, where it stopped

ph-kite.s: A kite does not flap wings. The wind lifts it. The kite is tilted. The wind pushes on its under side and shoves it up and back. The string does not let the wind carry the kite away. So the kite goes up instead of flying off. The push that lifts it up is called lift. It is the same push that holds aeroplanes in the sky. If there is no wind, you can run. Then the air rushes at the kite like wind.
a: A little bird drags it by the tail
It puffs itself up from laughing

ph-bubbles.s: A soap bubble is air inside a skin of water and soap. The skin is thinner than a hair. The skin always pulls tight, like a stretched elastic band. This is called surface tension. It tries to get as small as it can. The smallest skin to wrap some air is a ball. That is why bubbles are round, even if you blow them through a square frame! The water in the skin dries up, and the skin gets too thin. Then the bubble pops.
a: The skin pulls tight and becomes a ball
It has watched too many balls
It was blown up by little round buns

ph-shadow.s: Light travels in straight lines. When you block the sun, a shadow appears on the ground. In the morning the sun is low. The light comes from the side, and the shadow is very, very long. During the day the sun goes higher, and the shadow gets the shortest. In the evening the sun goes down again, and the shadow gets long again, but on the other side. The sun is not running across the sky. The Earth is slowly turning.
a: In the morning and in the evening
When you have eaten a lot of porridge
When the shadow put on its shoes

ph-echo.s: Sound is the air shaking, and it spreads out in every direction. When you shout “Hello-o!” in the yard, the sound flies to the wall of the house. It bounces off like a ball and comes back to you. That is an echo. Sound is very fast: in one second it goes more than three hundred metres. But it is not instant. So the echo comes back a little later. You hear it best when the big wall is far away.
a: Sound that bounced off a wall and came back
An invisible parrot around the corner

ph-puddle-boat.s: Why does a paper boat float in a puddle, but a pebble sinks? Water pushes up on everything that goes into it. The long name for this push is buoyancy. The more water a thing pushes aside, the bigger the push. A pebble is small but heavy. Even under the water, it does not get enough push. But a light, wide little boat floats until it gets wet through. Huge iron ships float in the same way. They have lots of air inside, and they push aside lots of water.
a: It has lots of air inside and pushes aside lots of water
Fish hold it up with a string

ph-sandbox.s: You cannot shape a sandcastle from dry sand. The grains roll off each other and fall apart. But if you make the sand a little wet, tiny bridges of water form between the grains. The water pulls together like the skin of a soap bubble. It pulls the grains close to each other, so the sandcastle keeps its shape. But with too much water, the bridges go away and the sand flows like porridge. The best sand is a little wet, but not dripping.
a: Sand that is a little wet
Sand that has been sung a little song

ph-tug-of-war.s: In tug of war, strong arms help, and so do strong legs. You hold your feet firm and push the ground forward. The ground pushes you back, and that is how you can pull. If your feet slide, your arm strength is wasted and you just get dragged along. What helps you hold on is friction, the rubbing between your shoes and the ground. Grippy shoes and dry grass are good. Ice is not. People who pull also lean back and put their feet wide apart.
a: The rubbing (friction) of your shoes on the ground

ph-warm-palms.s: Rub your hands together really fast. Can you feel them getting warm? Friction means things rubbing together, and it turns movement into heat. The same happens on a tube slide. You slide, your clothes rub against the plastic, and both get a tiny bit warm. After a slide like that, your hair sometimes stands on end. Rubbing makes a little electricity on you. The faster and harder you rub, the warmer it gets. That is why people rub their hands when it is very cold.
a: A tiny heater switched on inside
Your hands went red because they feel shy

msk-kuranty.s: There is a big clock on the Spasskaya Tower of the Kremlin. People call it the Kremlin Chimes. Every fifteen minutes it plays a tune, and at the start of every hour a big bell rings out the time. On New Year's Eve the whole country listens to the clock, makes wishes and welcomes the New Year. Above the clock shines a ruby star. It glows day and night and can turn in the wind like a weathervane.

msk-vasily.s: On Red Square stands St Basil's Cathedral. Its domes look like huge colourful onions. Every one is different, with its own pattern and its own colours. The cathedral was built more than four hundred years ago, in the time of Tsar Ivan the Terrible. And the square is not called Red because of its colour at all. In the old days the word “red” meant “beautiful”.

msk-tsar.s: Two giants stand in the Kremlin. The Tsar Cannon was made by the master Andrey Chokhov in 1586, but it was never fired in a war. The cannonballs next to it were put there much later, just for show. And the Tsar Bell is the biggest bell in the world. In a fire, a huge piece broke off it, so it has never rung. That piece still stands next to the bell today.
a: It is too shy to sing loudly

msk-metro.s: The Moscow Metro opened in 1935. Many of its stations look like palaces. They have big sparkly lamps, smooth stone and pictures made of tiny tiles. At Mayakovskaya station, look up! The ceiling shows a sky with aeroplanes, made of tiny tiles. At Revolution Square station there are bronze statues. One is a border guard with his dog. The dog's nose is shiny because people rub it for good luck.
a: People rub it for good luck

msk-bolshoi.s: The Bolshoi Theatre is one of the most famous theatres in the world. Above its tall pillars, four horses pull a chariot, and they are racing along. Apollo drives it. He was an ancient god who looked after the arts. On the stage of the Bolshoi Theatre, people dance ballet and sing opera. Right here, in 1877, Pyotr Tchaikovsky's ballet “Swan Lake” was shown for the first time.

msk-tretyakov.s: The trader Pavel Tretyakov spent his whole life collecting paintings by Russian artists. Then he gave them to Moscow. That is how the Tretyakov Gallery began. There hangs Ivan Shishkin's painting “Morning in a Pine Forest”. Three bear cubs play on a fallen pine tree, and their mother bear watches them. Shishkin painted forests wonderfully. His friend, the artist Konstantin Savitsky, helped him paint the bears.
a: The bears themselves, with their paws

msk-druzhba.s: At the Exhibition of Achievements of the National Economy stands the “Friendship of Peoples” fountain. In the middle rises a huge golden bunch of wheat and sunflowers. Around it stand sixteen golden girls. Each one wears the costume of her people and holds the gifts of her land. The fountain opened in 1954. When it works, hundreds of jets of water shoot up. Sometimes a rainbow shows in the spray.

msk-ostankino.s: The Ostankino TV Tower is the tallest tower in Europe. It is five hundred and forty metres high. TV and radio programmes are sent through the air from it. A fast lift takes visitors up to the top, where they can look out. The floor there is made of glass, and you can see the city right under your feet. On a cloudy day the top of the tower hides in the clouds.
a: A slide all the way to the ground

msk-reka.s: The Moskva River bends and curves through Moscow. The city got its name from the river, not the river from the city. In summer, little river trams sail along it, and from the deck you can see the walls of the Kremlin. Gorky Park is on the river bank. In winter a huge ice rink is made on its paths, and you can skate all over the park.

msk-panda.s: Moscow Zoo is more than a hundred and sixty years old. In 2019 two giant pandas came here from China, Ruyi and Dingding. They chew bamboo almost all day. Then they have a nice rest. And in 2023 they had a baby girl, Katyusha. She became the first giant panda born in Russia!

lon-big-ben.s: Everyone calls the tall clock tower in London Big Ben. But really, Big Ben is the name of the huge bell inside the tower. The bell weighs more than thirteen tonnes. Since 2012 the tower itself has been called the Elizabeth Tower. People set the clock's speed in a clever way. They put old coins on the pendulum, the big swinging weight. Add one more coin, and the clock runs a tiny bit faster.
a: The name of the royal dog

lon-ravens.s: The Tower of London is an old castle on the bank of the River Thames. The crowns and jewels of the British kings are kept there. Ravens live at the Tower too, always at least six of them. An old legend says that if the ravens fly away, something very bad will happen to the kingdom. The birds are looked after by a special Ravenmaster, and every raven has its own name.
a: A million and a tiny bit more

lon-guard.s: Buckingham Palace is the king's main palace in London. Soldiers in red coats and tall black fur hats guard it. The guards stand very straight. They do not look away, even when tourists take their photos. From time to time the guard changes. To the music of a band, some soldiers march in to take the place of others. Crowds of people gather to watch.
a: Ones with a pompom and bunny ears

lon-bus.s: Red buses with two floors run around London. It is best to sit upstairs, in the front row. From there you can see the city as if from a balcony. London also has famous black taxis, called cabs. To become a cab driver you have to learn thousands of streets by heart. It takes years, and the exam has a special name: “The Knowledge”.
a: How to fly on an umbrella

lon-tube.s: The London Underground is the oldest in the world. It opened in 1863. At first, steam engines pulled the trains. Londoners call the Underground “the Tube”, because many tunnels are round like a tube. At stations you often hear the words: “Mind the gap!” That means: watch your step, there is a gap between the train and the platform.

lon-eye.s: A huge Ferris wheel, the London Eye, turns by the River Thames. It has thirty-two glass cabins, one for each part of London. The wheel turns so slowly that people step into a cabin while it is moving. One circle takes about half an hour. The cabins are numbered from one to thirty-three. Number thirteen was skipped, because many people think it is unlucky.
a: Many people think this number is unlucky
The wind carried it off to the Moon

lon-tower-bridge.s: Tower Bridge opened in 1894. It has two tall stone towers. When a tall ship sails along the Thames, the middle of the bridge lifts. The two halves rise up like wings. High up between the towers there are paths with a glass floor, and through it you can see the cars driving below. Many people mix it up with London Bridge, but that is a completely different bridge.

lon-museum.s: The British Museum keeps treasures from all over the world, and it is free to go in. One of its best finds is the Rosetta Stone. The same words are carved on it in three kinds of writing. One kind is Egyptian hieroglyphs, and one is ancient Greek letters. Experts knew how to read Greek, so they could compare the writing. That is how people learned to read ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs.

lon-sherlock.s: Sherlock Holmes is a famous detective. The writer Arthur Conan Doyle made him up. In the books he lived in London, on Baker Street, at number two hundred and twenty-one B. Now there is a museum there. Its rooms are set up just like in the books. By Baker Street metro station stands a statue of the detective in a hat with two peaks. People from all over the world send letters to Sherlock as if he were real!

lon-greenwich.s: In Greenwich, a part of London, there is an old observatory, a place for watching the stars. A line runs across the ground there. It is called the prime meridian. People all over the world use it to measure how far east or west a place is. You can stand with one foot in the eastern half of the Earth and the other foot in the western half. There is a red ball on the roof of the observatory. Every day at exactly one o'clock it drops down. In the old days sailors used it to check their watches.

par-eiffel.s: The Eiffel Tower was built in 1889 for a big world fair. At first many people in Paris grumbled about it. Now it is the best-known sign of Paris. It is painted by hand, with brushes, about once every seven years. Every evening, at the start of each hour, the tower sparkles with thousands of lights for five minutes. At the very top, the engineer Gustave Eiffel had a little flat.
a: It jumps up and down on the spot

par-louvre.s: The Louvre is a huge museum in an old palace where French kings once lived. You go in through a big glass pyramid. In the Louvre hangs Leonardo da Vinci's painting “Mona Lisa”. Many people are surprised that it is quite small. The painting is kept behind thick glass, and crowds always gather in front of it to see her secret smile.
a: She can stick out her tongue

par-notre-dame.s: The Notre-Dame Cathedral stands on an island in the River Seine in Paris. Stone creatures with wings, little horns and funny faces look down at the city from its walls and towers. Some of them are gargoyles. They carry rain away: when it rains, water pours right out of their mouths. There was a fire, and the cathedral was mended for several years. It opened again in 2024.
a: Pour water out of their mouths

par-arc.s: Emperor Napoleon ordered the Arc de Triomphe to be built in 1806. It was to celebrate the wins of his army. It was only finished thirty years later. The arch stands in the middle of a round square. Twelve wide streets spread out from it like rays. That is why the square is called the Star Square. You can climb the stairs to the top of the arch and see the star from above.
a: Streets spread out from it like rays

par-montmartre.s: Montmartre is the highest hill in Paris. On its top stands the snow-white Sacré-Cœur church. It was built from a special stone that gets whiter in the rain. Nearby there is a little square where artists paint pictures, and pictures of people walking by, right in the street. Famous artists once lived in Montmartre, for example Pablo Picasso.
a: Paint pictures of people walking by

par-seine.s: Many bridges cross the Seine in Paris. The oldest one is called the New Bridge. It was finished more than four hundred years ago. Back then it really was new, and the name just stayed. Along the river, on the stone walls by the water, there are green boxes. In the daytime they are opened, and they turn into little stalls with old books, postcards and pictures.

par-baguette.s: A baguette is a long loaf of bread with a crunchy crust. It is hard to imagine Paris without it. Many people in Paris buy a fresh baguette every day. Every year Paris chooses the baker who bakes the best baguette. For a whole year he brings his bread to the president's palace. In 2022 the skill of baking baguettes was named a treasure of the whole world. And the croissant was named after its shape: in French the word means “crescent”, a thin curved moon.

par-versailles.s: Not far from Paris stands Versailles, the huge palace of the French kings. King Louis the Fourteenth, who was called the Sun King, made it so grand. When he was young, he danced the part of the Sun in a ballet, in a golden costume. In the palace there is the Hall of Mirrors, with hundreds of mirrors facing the tall windows. In the garden, fountains play, and sometimes they dance to music.

par-metro.s: The Paris Metro opened in 1900. The architect Hector Guimard designed the entrances to the old stations. They are made of green iron and look like plants from a fairy tale: curved stems, and lamps at the top like flower buds. Above the entrance is written “Métropolitain”. Many of these entrances are still there today, and they help you know at once that you are in Paris.

par-luxembourg.s: In the Luxembourg Garden in Paris there is a big pond with a fountain. You can rent a wooden boat with a sail there. Children push it with a long stick, and the wind carries the boat across the pond. When it sails to the other side, you have to run round the pond and push it again. Children have played like this in this garden for almost a hundred years.

rom-colosseum.s: The Colosseum was built in Rome almost two thousand years ago. It is a huge oval theatre without a roof, and it looks like a stone bowl. Tens of thousands of people came to watch fights between gladiators. On hot days a big cloth cover was stretched over the seats, like a sail. The floor was covered with sand. The word “arena” means “sand” in Latin.

rom-trevi.s: The Trevi Fountain is the most famous fountain in Rome. In the middle stands the stone god Oceanus. Sea horses pull his shell chariot. Here is what people do: stand with your back to the fountain and throw a coin over your shoulder. They say that then you will surely come back to Rome. The coins are collected later and given to help people who have a hard time.

rom-pantheon.s: The Pantheon is almost two thousand years old, and its huge dome is still in one piece. At the very top of the dome there is a round window with no glass. It is called the “oculus”, which means “eye”. A ray of sunlight comes in through it. When it rains, raindrops fall in too. The floor has little holes, so the water runs away and there are no puddles. Once a year, on a church holiday, rose petals are dropped from above through the oculus.

rom-wolf.s: An old legend says that the twin brothers Romulus and Remus started Rome. When they were tiny babies, their basket was carried away by the River Tiber. The basket got stuck at the bank, and a she-wolf found the babies. She did not hurt them. She fed them with her milk, like wolf cubs. Later a shepherd took the boys and looked after them. The city was named Rome after Romulus, and the she-wolf became its sign.

rom-vatican.s: Right inside Rome there is a whole country, the Vatican. It is the smallest country in the world. The Pope lives there. The ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in the Vatican was painted by the artist Michelangelo. He worked for about four years, standing on high wooden platforms with his head tipped back. When a new Pope is chosen, smoke comes out of the chimney above the chapel. White smoke means that a Pope has been chosen.
a: A new Pope has been chosen

rom-pisa.s: In the city of Pisa stands a white tower that leans to one side. It is a bell tower, with bells hanging at the top. People began to build it more than eight hundred years ago. It began to lean when only a few floors had been built, because the ground under it was soft. Engineers made the ground stronger and straightened the tower a tiny bit, so that it would not fall. Tourists love to take photos where it looks as if they are holding it up with one hand.
a: The ground beneath it is soft

rom-venice.s: Venice is built on water, on more than a hundred small islands. Instead of streets there are canals, which are streets of water. Instead of cars there are boats. The most famous boats are the black gondolas. The gondolier stands at the back and rows with one long oar. Here is the trick: the gondola is a bit crooked. One side of it is longer than the other. So it goes straight, even though the oar is only on one side.
a: None, he blows into a sail

rom-pizza.s: Pizza comes from the Italian city of Naples. There it is baked in a very hot oven with a wood fire, and the pizza is ready in less than two minutes. They say that one pizza was named after Queen Margherita. It has red tomatoes, white mozzarella cheese and green basil leaves. These are the colours of the Italian flag: green, white and red.

rom-pompeii.s: Near Naples stands the volcano Vesuvius. In the year 79 it woke up and buried the nearby city of Pompeii under a thick layer of ash. The city lay under the ground for more than fifteen hundred years, until people found it and began to dig it out. Now you can walk around Pompeii. You can see streets paved with stone, bakeries with ovens, and even a picture made of tiny tiles by the door of a house, with the words “Beware of the dog”.

rom-gelato.s: Italian ice cream is called gelato. Less air is mixed into it than into ordinary ice cream, so it is thick and very smooth. In Italian cafes it is often not scooped into a ball. It is served with a flat spatula, a flat tool like a little paddle. There are lots of flavours: pistachio, lemon, strawberry. There is also stracciatella, which is milk ice cream with bits of chocolate.

esp-sagrada.s: In Barcelona stands the Sagrada Família church. Antoni Gaudí planned it, and he worked on it for more than forty years. Building began more than a hundred and forty years ago, and it is still not finished! The pillars inside look like tree trunks, and rainbow light pours in through the coloured glass. In 2026 the tallest tower reached its full height, but the building work goes on.

esp-guell.s: Park Güell in Barcelona was planned by Gaudí too. On the stairs by the entrance sits a big lizard with many colours. Many people call it a dragon. It is covered with a pattern made from pieces of broken tile. The same kind of pattern covers a long bench that twists like a snake. The little houses by the entrance look like gingerbread houses, with roofs that seem to be covered with icing.

esp-alhambra.s: In the city of Granada, on a hill, stands the Alhambra. It is a palace and a castle. It was built by Muslim rulers who lived in Spain many hundreds of years ago. The name means “the red one”, because the castle walls are reddish. Inside, the walls are covered with carvings as fine as lace. In one courtyard there is a fountain. Its bowl is held up on the backs of twelve stone lions.
a: One, but a very strong one

esp-prado.s: Madrid is the capital of Spain. Here is one of the most famous museums in the world, the Prado. In it hangs Diego Velázquez's painting “Las Meninas”. In the middle stands the little Princess Margarita in a puffy dress. Around her are her maids, and a big dog lies in front. On the left, by a huge painting, stands the painter himself with a brush in his hand: he painted himself in the picture!

esp-flamenco.s: Flamenco began in the south of Spain, in Andalusia. It is song, guitar and dance all together. The dancer stands tall and proud. She spins in a big, puffy dress and taps out the beat loudly with her heels: tap-tap-tap! The others help by clapping their hands. Sometimes the dancers click castanets. These are wooden shells that you hold in your hands.

esp-paella.s: Paella comes from the Spanish city of Valencia. It is rice cooked in a wide flat pan, and the pan is also called “paella”. A spice called saffron makes the rice yellow. People put chicken, vegetables or sea creatures, such as prawns, in paella. At the bottom the rice gets a little fried and crunchy. Many people think this crunchy part is the tastiest.

esp-quixote.s: The writer Miguel de Cervantes made up Don Quixote, a funny and kind knight on a skinny horse called Rocinante. Don Quixote had read so many books about brave heroes that he decided to protect weak people himself. One day he saw some windmills and thought they were giants waving their arms. He charged at them with his spear! White windmills like these still stand on the hills of La Mancha.

esp-teide.s: The Canary Islands lie in the Atlantic Ocean, not far from Africa. On the island of Tenerife stands the volcano Teide, the highest mountain in Spain. In winter its top is sometimes covered with snow, while down by the sea it is warm. You can ride a cable car almost all the way to the top. The little singing bird, the canary, was named after these islands, where it lives in the wild.
a: After a sock with a hole in it

esp-tomatina.s: In the small Spanish town of Buñol, every year on the last Wednesday of August, there is the Tomatina festival. Thousands of people throw ripe tomatoes at each other! The rule is that you must squash a tomato in your hand before you throw it, so that nobody gets hurt. Soon the whole street turns red, like tomato soup. Then the streets are washed clean with big hoses.

esp-castells.s: In Catalonia, people build towers not out of stone but out of themselves. These living towers are called castells. Down below, many people stand close together in a crowd and hold up the people who stand on their shoulders. Level by level, the tower grows taller. A child in a safety helmet climbs to the very top and raises a hand: the tower is ready!

ger-brandenburg.s: The Brandenburg Gate is the best-known sign of Berlin. At the top stands a chariot pulled by four horses and driven by the goddess of victory. Once, the French emperor Napoleon took Berlin and carried this chariot away to Paris. But a few years later it was brought back. Since then, the horses have looked down on the city again from the top of the gate.
a: None, there is a bicycle there

ger-wall.s: Once, a long wall split Berlin in two. People on different sides could not freely visit each other, not even family. It was like that for almost thirty years. On the ninth of November 1989, the border was opened. People climbed on the wall, hugged, cried with joy and chipped off little pieces of the wall to keep. Now, where the wall once stood, a line of stones runs along the streets.
a: They built the wall even higher

ger-neuschwanstein.s: On a rock in the mountains of Bavaria stands the white Neuschwanstein Castle, just like a castle in a fairy tale. King Ludwig the Second ordered it to be built. He dreamed of knights and legends. The name of the castle means “New Swan Stone”. The king loved swans so much that there are swans everywhere in the castle, in paintings and in decorations. Even the water in the king's washbasin came from a silver tap shaped like a swan.

ger-grimm.s: The brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm published their first book of fairy tales more than two hundred years ago. They collected the tales from all sorts of people and carefully wrote them down. That is how “Snow White”, “Hansel and Gretel”, “Little Red Riding Hood” and “The Town Musicians of Bremen” got into their books. And in the city of Bremen there is a statue of the musicians: a dog on a donkey, a cat on the dog, and a rooster on top.

ger-xmas.s: Before Christmas, markets open in the squares of German towns. Little lights glow in the wooden huts, and the air smells of roasted almonds and gingerbread. Gingerbread is sold in the shape of hearts with messages written in icing. And there are wooden pyramids with a little fan at the top: warm air from burning candles turns them. Putting up and decorating a tree at Christmas also began in Germany.

ger-cologne.s: Builders began Cologne Cathedral in 1248. Then the work stopped for a long time. The cathedral was only finished in 1880, more than six hundred years later! For hundreds of years an old crane stood on the tower that was not finished. It became the sign of the city. The two pointed towers of the cathedral can be seen from far away. Inside, the windows made of coloured glass glow like huge glass pictures.

ger-cuckoo.s: In the south-west of Germany there are mountains covered with thick, dark forest. They are called the Schwarzwald, which means “Black Forest”. For more than two hundred years, cuckoo clocks have been made here. Every hour a little door opens, a wooden bird peeks out and calls: “Cuckoo!” Its voice comes from two small pipes and air pushed through them. The weights on these clocks are often shaped like fir cones.

ger-autobahn.s: The big fast roads in Germany are called autobahns. On many parts there are signs that tell you how fast you may drive. But there are also parts with no speed limit at all! This is very rare in the world. Still, drivers are advised not to go faster than one hundred and thirty kilometres an hour. And on the autobahn you may only pass other cars on the left.
a: No faster than one hundred and thirty kilometres an hour

ger-bach-beethoven.s: Two great music writers were born in Germany. Johann Sebastian Bach was born in 1685 in the city of Eisenach and was wonderful at playing the organ. Ludwig van Beethoven was born in 1770 in the city of Bonn. When Beethoven grew up, he could not hear well, and then he could hardly hear at all. But he kept on writing music! His tune “Ode to Joy” became the official song of Europe.

ger-pretzel.s: The pretzel is a German baked treat twisted into a knot. Before baking, it is quickly dipped in a special liquid. That is why the crust turns dark brown and shiny. Big grains of salt are sprinkled on top. People say its shape looks like arms folded across the chest. Above the doors of many bakeries in Germany hangs a sign in the shape of a pretzel.

nyc-liberty.s: People in France gave the Statue of Liberty to the Americans as a gift. It came to New York by sea in pieces, packed in crates. It was put together on an island. At first the statue was shiny and reddish, like a new penny, because it is made of copper. But the rain and the sea wind slowly turned the copper green. In her raised hand she holds a torch, and her crown has seven points like sunbeams.
a: The copper turned green from rain and wind
She was painted with green paint

nyc-empire-state.s: The Empire State Building is a famous skyscraper in New York. It has one hundred and two floors, and it was built in 1931. For almost forty years it was the tallest building in the world. On the eighty-sixth floor there is an open deck outside. From there, the cars far below look like toys. In the evenings the top of the skyscraper is lit up in different colours, for example on holidays.

nyc-central-park.s: Among the tall buildings in the middle of New York lies the huge Central Park. It is bigger than the whole country of Monaco! The park has a lake with boats, a zoo and a merry-go-round. In winter there is an ice rink. Busy squirrels run about everywhere. There is also a bronze statue of Alice in Wonderland, and children climb onto her giant mushroom.

nyc-brooklyn-bridge.s: The Brooklyn Bridge connects two parts of New York, Manhattan and Brooklyn. It opened in 1883, and it is held up by two stone towers and thick steel cables. At first, many people were afraid it would not hold. Then a circus owner led twenty-one elephants across the bridge! The bridge held, and everyone calmed down. People also stroll along a path above the cars.

nyc-yellow-taxi.s: Thousands of yellow taxis drive along the streets of New York. The bright yellow colour can be seen from far away, so you spot a taxi at once among the other cars. To stop a taxi, stand at the edge of the pavement and raise your hand. On the roof of the car there is a sign with a light. If the light is on, the taxi is free and you can get in.

nyc-dinosaurs.s: In New York there is the Museum of Natural History. Huge dinosaur skeletons stand there, and among them is a Tyrannosaurus. One dinosaur, the Titanosaur, is so long that it did not fit into the hall: its head peeks out into the corridor! In another hall, hanging from the ceiling, is a model of a blue whale as big as a real one. This whale is longer than two buses.
a: The tail of a yellow taxi

nyc-grand-canyon.s: The Grand Canyon is a giant, deep valley in the state of Arizona. The Colorado River cut it, and the river worked on it for millions of years. In places the canyon is more than one and a half kilometres deep. From above, the river at the bottom looks like a thin thread. The walls of the canyon are striped like a layer cake: each layer of rock formed in its own time. At sunset the cliffs turn red, orange and pink.

nyc-yellowstone.s: In 1872 Yellowstone became the first national park in the world. It is very hot under the ground there. Geysers burst out of the earth: they are fountains of hot water and steam. The most famous geyser is called Old Faithful. It shoots up so regularly that the park rangers can tell you in advance when to expect it. Nearby there are hot pools in all the colours of the rainbow. Tiny living things called microbes paint them. Bison walk slowly along the roads.
a: A fountain of hot water from under the ground

nyc-rushmore.s: In the state of South Dakota there is Mount Rushmore. The faces of four American presidents were cut right into the rock: George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Abraham Lincoln. Each face is about as tall as a six-storey building. The work lasted fourteen years, from 1927 to 1941. The extra rock was blown away, and then the workers carefully finished each face.
a: None, a bear is sleeping there

nyc-thanksgiving.s: On the fourth Thursday of November, America celebrates Thanksgiving. Families gather around a big table and say what they are thankful for. The main dish is roast turkey with cranberry sauce, and for pudding there is pumpkin pie. In the morning in New York there is a parade: huge balloons shaped like fairy-tale characters float above the streets. Each balloon is held on ropes by many people.

can-niagara.s: Niagara Falls is on the border of Canada and the USA. It is really three waterfalls. The biggest one is shaped like a horseshoe. The water crashes down with such a roar that a cloud of spray rises up, and you can often see a rainbow in it. Little boats sail up close to the falls, and every passenger gets a raincoat. In the evenings the falls are lit up with coloured lights.

can-cn-tower.s: In Toronto stands the CN Tower, which is five hundred and fifty-three metres tall. For many years it was the tallest tower in the world. A fast lift takes visitors to the top in less than a minute. And at three hundred and forty-two metres up there is a glass floor. You step onto it and, far below, you see the streets and tiny cars!
a: A glass floor high above the ground
A lift pulled by a horse
A trampoline right on the very top

can-maple.s: The flag of Canada has a red maple leaf on it. People make sweet maple syrup from the juice of the maple tree. This juice is called sap. In early spring, people put little tubes into the trees. The sap drips out drop by drop, and people collect it. Then it is boiled for a long time. It takes about forty litres of sap to make just one litre of syrup. Hot syrup is even poured onto clean snow. There it goes firm, and people wind it onto a stick like toffee.

can-beaver.s: The beaver is a sign of Canada. You can even see it on the five-cent coin. Beavers build dams on rivers. They use branches, logs and mud. They chew down trees with their strong orange teeth. Their teeth keep growing all their lives, so they never wear out. Moose live in the forests of Canada too. The moose is the biggest deer in the world. The males have antlers as wide as spades.

can-hockey.s: Ice hockey is the favourite winter game in Canada. The law says it is the national winter sport. In winter many families make an ice rink in their own garden. They pour water on the ground, and it freezes. Children chase the puck on frozen ponds. The puck is a flat, round piece of rubber. It flies very fast over the ice. One of the first ice hockey games indoors was played in Montreal, a city in Canada.

can-lake-louise.s: Lake Louise is high up in the Rocky Mountains. Its water is an amazing blue-green colour. The colour comes from the glaciers, which are huge rivers of ice. They grind rocks into tiny bits of stone dust. Streams carry the dust into the lake. The dust floats in the water and bounces back the sunlight in a special way. In winter the lake freezes. People skate on it, right in the middle of the mountains.

can-mounties.s: Some police in Canada ride horses, and they are famous. On holidays the police put on bright red uniforms, wide hats and tall boots. Today they travel by car, but they still keep their horses. The riders give a horse show with music. The horses move in lovely patterns. All the horses are black, so the red uniforms look even brighter.

can-two-languages.s: Canada has two main languages: English and French. So the writing on cereal boxes and milk cartons is in both languages. In a part of Canada called Quebec, most people speak French. There they say “bonjour” to say hello. In Toronto people more often say “hello”. Many Canadian children learn both languages at school.

can-northern-lights.s: On winter nights in the north of Canada, the sky sometimes glows. Green ribbons float and wave across it. Sometimes they have pink and purple edges. These are the northern lights. They happen when tiny bits from the Sun reach the Earth. They make the air high up in the sky glow. You can see the lights best on a clear, dark night, far from city lights.

can-polar-bears.s: The little town of Churchill is next to Hudson Bay. It is called the polar bear capital. Every autumn the bears come here. They wait for the sea to freeze. Then they walk over the ice to hunt seals. Visitors watch the bears from big trucks with huge wheels. Did you know that a polar bear's skin is black? Its fur is not white. It is see-through, but it looks white in the light.

cyp-aphrodite.s: A very long time ago, the Greeks told a story about Aphrodite. She was the goddess of love and beauty. She was born from the white foam of the sea near Cyprus. People still show the place where she came onto the land. It is a big rock in the sea, not far from Paphos. It is called Aphrodite's Rock. The waves crash on the stones and turn into white foam. Some people say that if you swim round the rock, you will become more beautiful.

cyp-turtles.s: In summer, at night, big sea turtles come onto the quiet beaches of Cyprus. They are called loggerhead turtles. The mother turtle digs a hole in the sand with her flippers. She lays eggs in it that look like ping-pong balls. About two months later, tiny baby turtles climb out of the sand. They run to the sea. The shiny sea under the moon shows them the way. That is why bright lamps are not switched on at night on these beaches.
a: To the top of a mountain

cyp-copper.s: A very long time ago, Cyprus was famous for its copper. People dug copper out of the ground there thousands of years ago. They sent it by ship to other countries. It was so famous that the Romans called it “Cyprian metal”. That gave us the Latin name for copper, “cuprum”. In science, the short name for copper is Cu. It still comes from this word.

cyp-mosaics.s: In 1962 a farmer in Paphos was ploughing his field. Suddenly he found old ruins. They were a Roman house! Its floors were covered in mosaics. A mosaic is a picture made of thousands of tiny coloured pebbles. These mosaics are about eighteen hundred years old! You can see ancient gods and heroes in them. You can see animals, birds and hunters too. The house is called the House of Dionysus. Today anyone can visit it.

cyp-kolossi.s: Kolossi Castle is not far from Limassol. It is a tall square tower with thick walls. Knights built it in 1454. The door is not at the bottom. It is on the second floor. A long time ago, you could only get in over a drawbridge. Inside, a narrow winding staircase goes all the way up to the roof. Next to the castle you can still see what is left of an old workshop. The knights made sugar there from sugar cane.

cyp-troodos.s: Cyprus is a hot island, but in winter there is snow in the Troodos Mountains. The highest mountain is called Olympus. Its ski lifts work, and children go skiing and sledging. From there you can drive to the warm sea in about an hour. In the mountain forests live mouflons. They are wild sheep with big curly horns. The mouflon is a sign of Cyprus. You can see it on coins from Cyprus.

cyp-halloumi.s: In Cyprus people make halloumi cheese from goat's milk and sheep's milk. It is not like other cheeses. In a frying pan, halloumi does not melt. It gets a golden-brown crust. When you chew it, it squeaks on your teeth! It is often sprinkled with mint. Halloumi is served with olives. Olive trees grow everywhere in Cyprus. Some of them live for hundreds of years.
a: It gets a crust but does not melt
It flies out of the window

cyp-carob.s: A carob tree grows in Cyprus. Long dark-brown pods hang from it. They look a bit like little horns. The pods are sweet. People boil them to make a thick syrup. The powder from the pods tastes a little like cocoa. Hard seeds are hidden inside the pods. In Greek, such a seed was called “keration”. That is where the word “carat” comes from. People still use it to weigh jewels.

cyp-nicosia.s: Nicosia is the capital of Cyprus. The old part of the city has walls shaped like a star. The star has eleven points. People from Venice built the walls more than four hundred years ago. From above, the city looks like a snowflake. For many years Nicosia has been split into two parts. In the middle of an old street with no cars, there is a crossing point. People calmly walk from one side to the other.

cyp-sea-caves.s: Near the town of Ayia Napa, the sea has made caves and arches in the pale cliffs. It took many years. The water there is so clear that you can see the stones on the bottom from a boat. Boats and kayaks go up to the caves. You can paddle a kayak under a stone arch called the Lovers' Bridge. Cape Greco is close by. There the sea sparkles blue and blue-green.

geo-legenda.s: There is an old story about Vakhtang, a king of Georgia. Once he went hunting with a falcon. The falcon chased a pheasant. Both birds vanished. Later they were found at a spring, where hot water was bubbling out of the ground. The king was amazed. He ordered a city to be built on that spot. It was named Tbilisi, from the Georgian word “tbili”, which means “warm”.

geo-bani.s: In old Tbilisi, hot water comes up out of the ground. It has sulphur in it. Bathhouses were built over it. From outside you can only see round brick roofs, like little hills. The water in the baths smells of boiled eggs, but it is lovely for warming up and resting. The poet Pushkin came here. He wrote that he had never seen anything better than these baths.

geo-narikala.s: High above old Tbilisi, on a mountain, stands the ancient Narikala Fortress. You can walk up to it. Or you can go up through the air! Glass cable cars start from a park next to the River Kura. They glide up to the fortress. They float right over the river and the roofs of the houses. From the top you can see the whole city. You can see bridges, round church roofs and colourful roofs.

geo-mat.s: On a hill above Tbilisi stands a huge silver statue of a woman. She is called Mother of Georgia. In one hand she holds a cup. In the other she holds a sword. The cup is to welcome people who come in peace. The sword is to keep the home safe from people who come to do harm. The statue tells us about the Georgians. They love guests, but they know how to stand up for themselves.
a: An umbrella and an ice cream
A fishing rod and a bucket

geo-bukvy.s: Georgian letters do not look like any other letters. They are round and curly, like little rings and snails. The Georgian alphabet has thirty-three letters. Sentences do not start with a capital letter. And there is a funny mix-up in the Georgian language. The word “mama” means Dad, and Mum is called “deda”.

geo-pesnya.s: Georgians love to sing in a choir with many voices. One voice sings the tune. The others sing higher and lower. The voices weave together like threads in a pattern. This kind of singing is counted as a treasure of the whole world. In 1977 an old song called “Chakrulo” was put on a golden record. It was sent into space on a spacecraft called Voyager. It is still flying among the stars.

geo-hachapuri.s: Khachapuri is a Georgian bread with cheese. Adjarian khachapuri looks like a little boat. The edges curl up. Inside there is hot, stretchy cheese. An egg is cracked on top, with a piece of butter. You break off the crispy edge and dip it in the middle. For pudding there is churchkhela. It is nuts on a string, covered in thick grape juice.

geo-kazbek.s: In the north of Georgia are the high Caucasus mountains. One of the most beautiful is Kazbek. Snow and ice lie on it all year round, even in hot summer. In Georgian, the name of this mountain means “icy peak”. Below Kazbek, on a high green hill, stands the old Gergeti church. Visitors walk up to it.

geo-mtskheta.s: Mtskheta is one of the oldest cities in Georgia. Long ago, the capital of the country was here. Two rivers, the Aragvi and the Kura, meet here. You can often see that their water is a different colour. On the mountain above them stands the ancient Jvari Monastery. In the town there is the great Svetitskhoveli Cathedral. The poet Lermontov wrote about these rivers: “Hugging like two sisters, the streams of the Aragvi and the Kura.”

geo-batumi.s: Batumi is on the shore of the Black Sea. A long path with palm trees runs along the sea. The beach here is not sandy. It is made of smooth pebbles. Every evening, two huge metal figures by the sea come to life. They are a young man and a young woman. They slowly move towards each other. They meet and pass through each other. It looks like magic!

arm-ararat.s: On a clear day, you can see the huge Mount Ararat from Yerevan. It has two tops: Greater Ararat and Lesser Ararat. The bigger one has snow on it all year round, sparkling in the sun. An old story says that after the Great Flood, Noah's Ark landed on this mountain with all the animals. Armenians love Ararat very much. They often paint it in pictures.
a: None, it is as flat as a pancake

arm-tuf.s: Yerevan is called the pink city. Many houses here are built of tuff. Tuff is a stone made from the ash of very old volcanoes. It can be pink, orange and even lilac. It is soft and easy to carve, so people carve patterns on it. In the evening, when the sun goes down, the walls glow with a warm pink light.

arm-bukvy.s: More than fifteen hundred years ago, the Armenians did not have their own letters. Then a wise monk called Mesrop Mashtots made up the Armenian alphabet. It has thirty-six letters. Since then, Armenians have written with their own letters, with hooks and tails. On the side of Mount Aragats there are big stone Armenian letters. They are almost as tall as a person. You can walk among them as if in a stone forest.

arm-matenadaran.s: In Yerevan there is a place called the Matenadaran. In Armenian this means “a place to keep books”. Thousands of old books are kept here. They were written by hand and have bright pictures in them. The biggest book weighs more than a five-year-old child. The smallest one fits easily on your hand. At the door stands a statue of Mesrop Mashtots, who made up the Armenian letters.
